_doc: Flagship transcript episode: Apollo 13 cryo-O2 tank failure. INPUT = the crew's real air-to-ground fault report (astronaut messages). BASELINE = the human mission-control loop that handled it, timestamps from the authoritative NASA record. METRIC = turns-to-diagnosis and time-to-diagnosis: from end of the astronaut fault report to the CapCom diagnosis. Numbers marked VERIFY are provisional (OCR-estimated) and must be reconciled against the full AFJ air-to-ground transcript before becoming a paper result.
corpus_relation: in-corpus (Apollo 13 is the reference corpus) — flagship, not a cross-mission scenario

input_utterances.speaker: CMP
input_utterances.text: Okay, Houston, we've had a problem here.

input_utterances.speaker: CDR
input_utterances.text: Houston, we've had a problem. We've had a MAIN B BUS UNDERVOLT.

input_utterances.speaker: LMP
input_utterances.text: Okay. Right now, Houston, the voltage is looking good. And we had a pretty large bang associated with the caution and warning there. And as I recall, MAIN B was the one that had an amp spike on it once before.

input_utterances.speaker: CDR
input_utterances.text: And, Houston, we had a RESTART on our computer and we had a PGNCS light and the RESTART RESET.
input_utterances.note: content verbatim from transcript OCR; GET seconds not yet reconciled

input_utterances.speaker: CDR
input_utterances.text: We're looking at our SERVICE MODULE RCS HELIUM 1. We have B is barber poled and D is barber poled.

input_utterances.speaker: LMP
input_utterances.text: MAIN A UNDERVOLT now, too. It's reading about 25-1/2, MAIN B is reading zip right now.

input_utterances.speaker: CDR
input_utterances.text: And, Jack, our O2 QUANTITY number 2 tank is reading zero.

input_utterances.speaker: CDR
input_utterances.text: And it looks to me, looking out the hatch, that we are venting something. We are venting something out into space. It's a gas of some sort, coming out of window 1.
input_utterances.note: the visual venting cue that let mission control finally characterize the failure (~14 min after the incident)

input_note: MULTI-TURN evidence stream: the crew's real air-to-ground utterances in GET order, one per diagnostic turn. Lodestar replays them one at a time, accumulating evidence, and we record the turn at which it converges on the diagnosis (turns-to-diagnosis) vs the human loop. This is the SAME evidence the humans had, including the venting cue at turn 7 — if Lodestar converges before turn 7 (from the electrical picture alone) that is the 'beats the human loop' result; if it needs the venting cue too, that is reported honestly.

human_baseline.report_end_note: end of Lovell's 55:55:35 fault report (~a few seconds); this is t=0 for time-to-diagnosis

checkpoints.name: receipt
checkpoints.meaning: CapCom acknowledges receipt of the fault. NOT a diagnosis — the lower bound / comms floor.

checkpoints.name: diagnostic_recognition
checkpoints.capcom_text: Roger. We copy your venting.  (CapCom confirms the failure is real O2 venting, not an instrumentation glitch)
checkpoints.meaning: First point at which the failure is correctly CHARACTERIZED as O2 loss / real venting rather than a suspected electrical/instrumentation transient. Documented as ~14 min after the incident.
checkpoints.delta_note: ~13-14 min; authoritative record states venting observed ~14 min after incident

checkpoints.name: stabilizing_plan
checkpoints.scope: OUT OF SCOPE — the contribution is reduction to DIAGNOSIS, not resolution-plan generation. Kept only as historical context / an informational secondary checkpoint.
checkpoints.capcom_text: powerdown to G&C checklist pink pages 1-5; subsequently power up the LM as a lifeboat
checkpoints.meaning: CapCom issues the corrective PLAN grounded in the true failure (preserve the CM, move to the LM lifeboat).
checkpoints.delta_note: documented on the order of 1.5-2 h to the LM power-up decision; exact CapCom GET must be reconciled from the AFJ air-to-ground transcript

turns_to_diagnosis.to_diagnostic_recognition_note: the human loop characterized the failure correctly only at the 8th crew evidence turn (the visual venting cue at ~56:09); the seven prior electrical/systems turns — including O2 QUANTITY 2 reading zero at turn 7 — did not suffice for the ground to conclude a real O2 loss rather than instrumentation
turns_to_diagnosis.note: human turns-to-diagnosis = index of the crew evidence turn by which the diagnosis was reached (crew utterances are the shared evidence stream both sides see)

resolution_anchor._source: Report of Apollo 13 Review Board (Cortright Commission), 1970; NASA mission report. Standard historical record.
resolution_anchor.symptom: Master alarm with MAIN BUS B (then A) UNDERVOLT shortly after a cryo-tank stir; loud bang; computer RESTART / PGNCS light; SM RCS helium indications; O2 quantity 2 reading zero; two of three fuel cells lost.
resolution_anchor.documented_cause: Cryogenic oxygen tank no. 2 in the service module failed (insulation on fan wiring, damaged before flight, ignited during the stir), rupturing the tank and the SM bay. Loss of O2 caused fuel cells 1 and 3 to fail, dropping main buses B and A. The CSM lost its primary power and oxygen source.
resolution_anchor.corrective_action: Power down the Command/Service Module to preserve reentry consumables; power up the Lunar Module (Aquarius) from its descent-stage batteries and use it as a lifeboat for life support, power, and propulsion during the return; manage water/O2/power consumables for the return trajectory.
